prompt:
Moral Foundations Theory is a framework that separates human morality into the following categories:

  - Care/Harm: related to our long evolution as mammals with attachment systems
    and an ability to feel (and dislike) the pain of others. It underlies the
    virtues of kindness, gentleness, and nurturance.

  - Loyalty/Betrayal: related to our long history as tribal creatures able to
    form shifting coalitions. It is active anytime people feel that it is "one
    for all and all for one." It underlies the virtues of patriotism and
    self-sacrifice for the group.

  - Authority/Subversion: shaped by our long primate history of hierarchical
    social interactions. It underlies virtues of leadership and followership,
    including deference to prestigious authority figures and respect for
    traditions.

  - Sanctity/Purity: shaped by the psychology of disgust and contamination. It
    underlies notions of striving to live in an elevated, less carnal, more
    noble, and more "natural" way (often present in religious narratives). This
    foundation underlies the widespread idea that the body is a temple that can
    be desecrated by immoral activities and contaminants (an idea not unique to
    religious traditions). It underlies the virtues of self-discipline,
    self-improvement, naturalness, and spirituality.

  - Equality: related to our intuitions about equal treatment and equal outcome
    for individuals.

  - Proportionality: related to our intuitions about individuals getting
    rewarded in proportion to their merit or contribution.

TEXT_D:
UKIP Manifesto 2015 — Summary (ideological framing preserved)

UKIP offers a serious, fully costed plan to restore British sovereignty, control our borders, cut waste, and invest in frontline services without raising taxes or debt. By leaving the EU, scrapping HS2, reducing overseas aid to 0.2% of GNI, ending health tourism, replacing the Barnett Formula, and cutting government waste and quangos, UKIP funds: £12bn extra for the NHS, £5.2bn for social care, 6,000 extra police/prison/Border staff, defence back to 2%+ of GDP, tax cuts for workers, and reliefs for small firms and families.

Economy and tax
- Raise the personal allowance to at least £13,000; take the minimum wage out of income tax; lift the 40% threshold to £55,000; add a 30% band; abolish inheritance tax; increase transferable married/civil partner allowance.
- Tackle multinational tax avoidance by restoring UK tax sovereignty.
- Replace the Barnett Formula with a needs-based system; reduce Whitehall and quangos.

Immigration
- Immigration is about space, not race. Leave the EU to end free movement.
- Five-year moratorium on unskilled immigration; Australian-style points system treating all nations fairly.
- Count all entries/exits; +2,500 Border Force; no amnesty; five years’ contributions before full benefits/NHS (beyond urgent care); tougher action on sham marriages and foreign criminals; revoke citizenship for terrorists.

NHS and social care
- 8,000 more GPs, 20,000 nurses, 3,000 midwives; GPs in A&E; £1.5bn for mental health and dementia; free hospital parking.
- End health tourism; licence NHS managers; abolish PFI; scrap damaging EU directives; exclude the NHS from TTIP.
- Restore social care by £1.2bn, integrate with the NHS, introduce a Dignity Code; boost carers’ allowance by £572.

Welfare and pensions
- Flexible state pension window; better pensions advice; ban pension cold-calling.
- Scrap the bedroom tax; GP/specialist-led disability assessments; cap benefits; end welfare tourism.

Education
- More parental choice: grammar, vocational, technical schools; abolish KS1 SATs; cut teacher workload.
- Age-appropriate sex education at secondary only; first aid in PSHE.
- Reverse special school closures; streamline Ofsted.
- Waive tuition fees for UK STEMM students who work in the UK five years.

Housing and environment
- Prioritise brownfield: stamp duty relief on first £250k for new brownfield homes; bring empty homes into use.
- Protect green belt; restrict social housing and Help to Buy to citizens/5-year contributors; homelessness register.

Transport
- Scrap HS2; support re-opening Manston Airport.
- Speed cameras only for safety; oppose road pricing/eCall; end tolls; fairer HGV levies on foreign trucks.

Energy
- Repeal the Climate Change Act; end subsidies for onshore wind/solar; back shale, coal, nuclear and hydro; abolish green levies and EU ETS to cut bills.

Jobs and small business
- Prefer British workers; enforce minimum wage; zero-hours code to stop abuse.
- 20% business rates cut for premises under £50k RV; punish big firms for late payment; expand trade credit insurance; 30 minutes free town-centre parking; slash EU red tape; open public contracts.

Farming, fishing, animal welfare
- New capped per-acre Single Farm Payment; support dairy/sheep; honest food labelling.
- Ban live exports; CCTV in abattoirs.
- Leave CFP; 200-mile UK EEZ; end destructive industrial fishing; prioritise under-10m fleet and sea angling.

Law, order, justice
- +6,000 frontline police/prison/Border posts; leave ECHR, enact a UK Bill of Rights; scrap EU arrest measures.
- Deport foreign offenders; decriminalise TV licence non-payment; modernise sentencing for cyber/sex trafficking/knife and weapon crimes.

Political reform and localism
- Citizen-initiated national referendums; real right of recall; open primaries.
- Select committee vetoes on major appointments and spending lines.
- Proportional voting with constituency link; restrict general election voting to citizens; end postal voting on demand.
- Binding local referenda on major developments; weekly bins; zero-tolerance on ASB.

Culture, heritage, pubs, tourism
- Promote British values and integration; English (plus Welsh/Gaelic) for official documents; defend free speech; mandatory FGM reporting.
- Remove VAT on listed-building repairs; presumption in favour of conservation; regenerate seaside towns; save pubs (optional smoking rooms; oppose minimum pricing).

Trade, defence, aid, Brexit
- Leave the EU via Article 50; bespoke UK–EU free-trade deal; WTO MFN; global trade deals.
- Defence to 2%+ GDP; retain Trident; crew carriers; tax-free pay on operations; unify intelligence; oppose an EU army.
- Cut aid to 0.2% GNI; close DfID and focus on clean water, vaccines, disaster relief; trade not aid.

Believe in Britain.

TEXT_F:
Labour’s 2015 manifesto sets out a plan to make Britain work for working people, anchored by a Budget Responsibility Lock: every promise is fully funded with no new borrowing; the deficit will be cut every year; national debt will fall and the current budget return to surplus as soon as possible, independently verified by the OBR. The core belief: Britain only succeeds when working families succeed—through fair rewards for work, strong public services, and power devolved to communities.

Economic foundations and fair taxes
- Restore fiscal credibility while tackling the causes of the deficit through higher productivity and rising living standards.
- Fairer taxes: restore the 50p top rate; introduce a 10p starting rate funded by ending the Marriage Allowance; abolish non-dom status; no rises in basic or higher Income Tax, NI or VAT; tough action on avoidance.
- Back small business: cut and then freeze business rates for 1.5m small firms; create a British Investment Bank and regional banks; boost competition in banking; levy payday lenders to support credit unions.
- Long-term growth: National Infrastructure Commission; HS2 with cost control and better northern rail; strategic roads and cycling; swift airport decision; universal affordable high-speed broadband and better mobile coverage.
- Lead the low-carbon transition: legal 2030 decarbonised power target; empower the Green Investment Bank; Energy Security Board; one million new green jobs.

Better work, pay and chances for young people
- Raise the National Minimum Wage to £8+ by Oct 2019; promote the Living Wage via procurement and Make Work Pay contracts; require listed firms to report Living Wage status.
- Ban exploitative zero-hours contracts and close the agency worker loophole; scrap employment tribunal fees.
- Rebalance corporate governance to favour long-termism, curb excessive pay, and give employees a voice.
- Create a gold-standard technical route: Technical Baccalaureate and Technical Degrees; guarantee an apprenticeship for every school leaver with the grades; cut tuition fees to £6,000; end unpaid internships lock-out. Fund a Compulsory Jobs Guarantee via a bank bonus tax.

Cutting the cost of living and fixing broken markets
- Freeze energy bills until 2017 and reform the market with a tough new watchdog; drive energy efficiency.
- Water affordability scheme and stronger regulation.
- Rail reform with a public operator option; fare freeze then strict caps; powers for city/region-wide integrated transport.
- Build at least 200,000 homes a year by 2020; first call for local first-time buyers; new garden cities; tackle land banking.
- Fair renting: three-year tenancies the norm, cap excessive rent rises, ban letting fees. Abolish the Bedroom Tax.
- Family support: free childcare rising from 15 to 25 hours for working parents of 3–4-year-olds; guarantee wraparound care 8am–6pm; double paternity leave to four weeks and increase pay.

World-class NHS and care, and high-quality education
- Rescue the NHS: 20,000 more nurses, 8,000 more GPs, 3,000 more midwives funded by a Mansion Tax, a tobacco levy and anti-avoidance; 48-hour GP appointments; one-week cancer tests.
- Repeal the Health and Social Care Act; NHS preferred provider; cap private profits; integrate physical, mental and social care; parity for mental health; focus on prevention.
- End 15-minute care visits; recruit 5,000 home-care workers; support carers.
- Protect the entire education budget; all teachers qualified; cap infant class sizes at 30; new School Standards Directors; boost vocational excellence.

Safe, cohesive communities with fair immigration
- Protect neighbourhood policing (safeguard over 10,000 officers); a Victims’ Law; tougher action on domestic abuse and child exploitation; ban legal highs.
- Counter extremism with community-led Prevent, stronger oversight, and proportionate powers.
- Controlled, fair immigration: 1,000 extra border staff, full exit checks, two-year wait for benefits, English requirement for public-facing roles; ban wage undercutting and rogue agencies.

Power closer to people and rights protected
- English Devolution Act: £30bn and major powers to city and county regions; local Public Accounts Committees; Constitutional Convention; replace the Lords with a Senate of the Nations and Regions; votes at 16.
- Clean politics: tougher lobbyist register; ban MPs’ paid directorships; extend FOI; media plurality and full Leveson implementation; protect the Human Rights Act; require large firms to publish gender pay gaps; race equality strategy. Keep Channel 4 public; free museum entry; give fans a voice in football clubs.

Britain in the world
- Reform the EU from within; lock any future power transfers behind a referendum; uphold NATO; defence review; maintain a minimum credible nuclear deterrent; strengthen cyber security.
- Lead on climate change towards global net zero in the second half of the century.
- Keep 0.7% aid, focus on the poorest, support universal health coverage.

A fully funded, credible plan to rebuild a fairer, more secure Britain—together.
